cases.title: Initiate drag event on product item capturing title and price
cases.description: Verify that dragging a product item (li element with draggable='true' and data-testid='product-item-1') initiates a drag event and captures the product's title and price for transfer using its data-testid identifiers such as 'product-title-1' and 'product-price-1'.

cases.title: Drop product into drop area to add to cart
cases.description: Verify that dragging and dropping a product item (e.g., data-testid="product-item-1") into the designated drop area (id="div1", data-testid="drop-area") updates the cart display automatically: the product title appears in .box2, the unit price in .box3, and the quantity in .box1.

cases.title: Add repeated products to the cart
cases.description: Verify that dropping the same product item multiple times into the drop area updates the cart display correctly to support repeated products.

cases.title: Calculate and display total price in allMoney element
cases.description: Verify that the system calculates the total price by summing the prices of all products in the cart, formats the total to two decimal places with the appropriate currency symbol (e.g., '$80.00'), and displays it in the <div id="allMoney"> element.

opinions.feedback: All requirements and explicit scenarios are fully covered by the proposed test cases. No missing scenarios or blockers found.
All requirements and cases have been reviewed. The cases correctly cover the specified scenarios for dragging, dropping, adding both different and repeated products, and calculating the total price.

coverage.feedback: The accepted cases provide solid and direct coverage of the explicit requirements (R-1, R-3, and R-5). Specifically, G-001 correctly tests the drag event capturing title and price for R-1. G-002 and G-003 cover dropping single and repeated products into the drop area and updating the cart UI (.box1, .box2, .box3) satisfying R-3. G-004 appropriately validates total price calculation and formatting in the #allMoney element for R-5. There are no notable coverage gaps, and the cases avoid overgeneration or speculative edge cases beyond the stated requirements.
